issues.legal_issue: Excluding debts from a debt-reduction scheme according to the identity of the creditor violates equality when that classification has no rational relationship to the scheme’s objective.
material_facts: The law aimed to reduce debts secured on property that had been resumed, because resumption reduced the property holders’ capacity to pay.
The law excluded debts owed to specified public bodies and other categories of creditors, while leaving other private debts within the scheme.
The excluded categories had no discernible common principle, and creditor identity had no rational relationship to the objective of reducing debts secured on resumed property.
issues.conclusion: The creditor-based exclusions were invalid because no reasonable classification justified them under the equality guarantee.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits classification only when it rests on an intelligible differentia distinguishing the included group from those left out and that differentia has a rational relationship to the statute’s objective. The Court relied on this test and distinguished Manna Lal v. Collector of Jhalwar, which concerned a special facility for recovery of government-owned bank debts; it disagreed with the reasoning in Nand Ram Chhotey Lal v. Kishore Raman Singh and found Jamnalal Ramlal Kimtee v. Kishendas and State of Hyderabad unpersuasive because it did not address the required rational relationship.

rule.if: constitutional_validity_challenge and debt_relief_targets_resumed_property_debts and exclusions_turn_on_creditor_identity and (exemptions_have_no_common_principle or creditor_status_unrelated_to_relief_objective)

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A party challenged the constitutionality of a law in a proceeding concerning debt relief.
predicates.debt_relief_targets_resumed_property_deb: The law sought to reduce debts secured on property taken over by the state, where that taking reduced the debtor’s capacity to pay.
predicates.exclusions_turn_on_creditor_identity: The law excluded debts according to the identity or category of the creditor.
predicates.exemptions_have_no_common_principle: The excluded creditor categories did not share a discernible principle distinguishing them from creditors whose debts remained covered.
predicates.creditor_status_unrelated_to_relief_obje: The identity or status of the creditor had no rational connection to the law’s objective of reducing debts secured on resumed property.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns debt relief for debts secured on resumed property, exclusions based on creditor identity violate equality if the exempted groups lack a common principle or creditor status is unrelated to the relief objective.

issues.legal_issue: Limiting recovery of a reduced secured debt to compensation for resumed property is a reasonable restriction in the general public interest when it supports the rehabilitation of the affected debtor.
material_facts: The law reduced debts secured on resumed property and limited recovery of the reduced amount to compensation and a rehabilitation grant payable for that property.
The property had been taken over for a public purpose at a low valuation.
The secured creditor had primarily looked to the secured property for repayment.
Without the recovery limit, the debtor’s other property, future income, and later-acquired property could be reached, making it difficult to start life afresh.
issues.conclusion: The recovery limit was valid because it imposed a reasonable restriction in the general public interest on the rights of a secured creditor.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7(2) of the Rajasthan Jagirdars’ Debt Reduction Act was valid as a reasonable restriction in the interest of the general public on secured-creditor rights. The Court relied on the provision’s rehabilitative purpose, the public-purpose resumption of the secured property at a low valuation, and the fact that the creditor had primarily relied on that property for repayment. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A party challenged the constitutionality of a law in a proceeding concerning debt relief.
predicates.reduced_secured_debt_concerns_resumed_pr: The debt was secured on property taken over by the state and was reduced under a debt-relief scheme.
predicates.recovery_is_limited_to_property_compensa: The law confined recovery of the reduced debt to compensation or a rehabilitation payment for the resumed property.
predicates.resumption_served_public_purpose: The state took over the secured property for a public purpose and valued it low enough to make rehabilitation relevant.
predicates.broader_recovery_would_reach_other_asset: Without the recovery limit, enforcement could reach the debtor’s other property, future income, or later-acquired property and hinder a fresh start.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns reduced debt secured on resumed property, limiting recovery to compensation for that property is valid if the resumption served a public purpose and broader recovery would reach the debtor’s other assets.
